liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Drums** (1 review): Jerry stays on stage and plays a few notes at the start of Drums [31]
- **Spoonful** (1 review): The transition from He's Gone into Spoonful is singled out as especially good [32]
- **Samson & Delilah** (1 review): Weir forgot to switch on his mic until the second verse of Samson [32]
- **Bertha** (1 review): Jerry's Bertha, along with Althea, Ramble On Rose and Deal, is called excellent, with his voice in top form [39]
- **Mexicali Blues** (1 review): Mexicali Blues gets a nice workout with an extended jam [39]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd85-03-24 s1 t01 Bertha**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [40]
- **gd85-03-24 s1 t02 Promised Land**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [40]
- **gd85-03-24 s1 t03 Althea**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [40]
- **gd85-03-24 s1 t04 Me & My Uncle**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [40]
- **gd85-03-24 s1 t05 Mexicali Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [40]
- **gd85-03-24 s1 t06 Ramble On Rose**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [40]
- **gd85-03-24 s1 t07 New Minglewood Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [40]
- **gd85-03-24 s1 t08 Deal**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [40]

## The recordings

- **gd1985-03-24.140840.unknown.bryant.miller.clugston.flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 20 songs; 136 min [1]
- **gd85-03-24.oade.connor.8461.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 139 min; rated 3.93/5 by 14 [5]. Said about its sound: Audience recording by Oade is very listenable, though a bit weaker than his tapes from the following week or so [28]
- **gd1985-03-24.169120.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 136 min [6]
- **gd1985-03-24.167065.beyer.m160.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 136 min [8]
- **gd1985-03-24.164362.nak304.thomas.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 137 min [10]
- **gd85-03-24.sbd-set2.willy.11699.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 12 songs; 78 min; rated 4/5 by 6 [27]. Said about its sound: Soundboard of set two is clean and well rounded, with no significant flaws [32]

## Around the show

- Reviewer had tickets to the whole run and recalls a nice crowd and a beautiful day and night [33]
- Small arena, perhaps 11K capacity, with blue gels, bitterly cold outside, blistering hot inside, and lots of band-audience chatter [34]
- Reviewer's first tour began with this run; the show served to get the joints oiled [36]
- Reviewer attended with friends who were first-timers; songs seemed to flow into each other [37]
- The reviewer ranks the whole March/April 1985 run among the decade's best [28]
- The 3/31/85 show has a similar Jerry lead-in to Drums, recommended as a real treat [31]
- This was the last of the Springfield shows; both nights were epic [34]
- The following night is described as a meeting of the tribe, making this a good setup for a two-night stand [37]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1985-03-24.140840.unknown.bryant.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Robert Bryant; transferred by Charlie Miller and Scott Clugston; source: Source Info: Robert Bryant's Master Audience Cassettes; unknown mics > Sony TC-D5M; Transfer Info: Master Cassettes (Nakamichi CR-7A)> Tascam DA-3000 (DSF… [1]. Also: A Schoeps CMC4/MK41 source (shnid 8461) supplies a 21-second patch in Drums [1]
- **gd85-03-24.oade.connor.8461.sbeok.shnf**: source: Oade's Master Audience PCM>Schoeps CMC-441 mics>Oade M118>Sony PCM-F1>DAT>CDR>EAC>ShnEAC'ed/Shn'ed and seeded to fungus and abgd by Charlie Connor 3/26/02 with… [5]
- **gd1985-03-24.169120.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Michael Hessberg; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Michael Hessberg's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser ME-80 mics > Sony D5M [6]. Also: Oade Schoeps CMC4/MK41 source patches 12 seconds in Deal, 23 seconds in Drums, and supplies the whole U.S. Blues encore [6]
- **gd1985-03-24.167065.beyer.m160.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Beyer M160 mics > Sony D5M (Maxell XLII-S) [8]. Also: A Sennheiser 441 source from Rob Hunt and Ted Mattes patches 8 seconds of the Dear Mr. Fantasy to Throwing Stones transition [8]
- **gd1985-03-24.164362.nak304.thomas.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Stephen Thomas; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Stephen Thomas' Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 300 mics + CP4 shotguns > Sony D5M [10]. Also: Sennheiser 441 source from Hunt and Mattes supplies the start of New Minglewood Blues and two patches in Drums [10]
- **gd85-03-24.sbd-set2.willy.11699.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD>?>CD [27]

claims.text: Audience recording by Oade is very listenable, though a bit weaker than his tapes from the following week or so
The reviewer ranks the whole March/April 1985 run among the decade's best
Jerry stays on stage and plays a few notes at the start of Drums
The 3/31/85 show has a similar Jerry lead-in to Drums, recommended as a real treat
Soundboard of set two is clean and well rounded, with no significant flaws
The transition from He's Gone into Spoonful is singled out as especially good
Weir forgot to switch on his mic until the second verse of Samson
Reviewer had tickets to the whole run and recalls a nice crowd and a beautiful day and night
Small arena, perhaps 11K capacity, with blue gels, bitterly cold outside, blistering hot inside, and lots of band-audience chatter
This was the last of the Springfield shows; both nights were epic
Reviewer's first tour began with this run; the show served to get the joints oiled
Reviewer attended with friends who were first-timers; songs seemed to flow into each other
The following night is described as a meeting of the tribe, making this a good setup for a two-night stand
Reviewer rates set one above set two, calling the first set wild and thick with energy
Jerry's Bertha, along with Althea, Ramble On Rose and Deal, is called excellent, with his voice in top form
Jerry sings little in set two: only two songs plus the U.S. Blues encore
Mexicali Blues gets a nice workout with an extended jam
Master audience cassette from Robert Bryant, transferred by Charlie Miller
A Schoeps CMC4/MK41 source (shnid 8461) supplies a 21-second patch in Drums
Master cassette recorded by Michael Hessberg, transferred by Charlie Miller, using a Sennheiser ME80 microphone setup
Oade Schoeps CMC4/MK41 source patches 12 seconds in Deal, 23 seconds in Drums, and supplies the whole U.S. Blues encore
Master cassettes from Jim Vita, transferred by Charlie Miller, recorded with Beyer M160 microphones
A Sennheiser 441 source from Rob Hunt and Ted Mattes patches 8 seconds of the Dear Mr. Fantasy to Throwing Stones transition
Sennheiser 441 source from Hunt and Mattes supplies the start of New Minglewood Blues and two patches in Drums
